questions.question: When is zero-shot mentioned?
questions.answer: Zero-shot is first listed alongside one-shot as the fifth technique used to render a prompt secure and stable [1]. It is later defined as prompting the LLM without giving it any real examples of what needs to be done [2]. Finally, it is mentioned again during a practical example, noting that omitting examples from your prompt is called zero-shot [3].

claims.claim: Zero-shot is first listed alongside one-shot as the fifth technique used to render a prompt secure and stable.
claims.evidence: And the fifth, fifth, fifth is Zero-Shot or One-Shot... These six techniques you should use if you want to make your prompt completely secure and stable.

claims.claim: It is later defined as prompting the LLM without giving it any real examples of what needs to be done.
claims.evidence: If you don't give any example, if you omit this, then it is called zero shot, meaning you are not explaining to the LLM by giving any example of what needs to be done.

claims.claim: Finally, it is mentioned again during a practical example, noting that omitting examples from your prompt is called zero-shot.
claims.evidence: If you didn't write examples right now, what would that be called? Zero-shot. There are no examples.
